thread.title: Dow Stocks Keep Losses Small; Citigroup Reverses Up | Investor's Business Daily

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Dow Stocks Keep Losses Small; Citigroup Reverses Up | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Blue chips showed the smallest losses Monday morning even as Apple ( AAPL ) weighed among Dow stocks. In the meantime, Citigroup ( C ) staged a positive reversal.
X The Dow Jones industrial average dropped 0.4%, while the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 fell 0.8% and 0.6% respectively. The Russell 2000 small-cap index slipped 0.7%.
Volume was quiet on both major exchanges.
Citigroup launched earnings season with mixed results. Earnings for the fully year 2018 rose 25%, according to William O'Neil + Co. data — a good follow-up to 2017's 20% earnings growth. Citigroup's back-to-back earnings gains of 20% and 25% were the best since 1999-2000.
But Citigroup's fixed-income revenue was weaker than expected. Citigroup dropped 1.7% in the first five minutes of trade but then staged a positive reversal. In late morning trade, the stock was up 3.6%.
Lululemon Up Sharply Meanwhile, retail apparel stocks were among the day's strongest movers. Lululemon Athletica ( LULU ) gapped up 9% in heavy volume on raised guidance. The stock is 12% off its high.
Lululemon is building the right side of a consolidation. The stock is trading above its 10-week moving average line. It was added to the Leaderboard watch list Monday.
American Eagle Outfitters ( AEO ) climbed 2.5% in heavy volume. The stock is above its 10-week line but 31% off its high.
Elsewhere, footwear and apparel provider Boot Barn ( BOOT ) gapped up 13% in torrid volume. The stock remains about 30% off its high.
Going into Monday's session, the retail sector was up 5.8% so far in 2019.
Dow Stocks On The Move Among Dow Jones stocks, Apple fell 1.5% Monday morning in below-average volume. The stock has dropped in 12 of the past 15 weeks and is 35% off its high. Analysts expect earnings growth to drop to 2% in fiscal 2019 ending in September. The 2% EPS growth would be Apple's third worst performance in the past 16 years.
Stock Sector Changes Although it's early in 2019, some stocks are making a grab at leadership. In the first eight trading days of 2019, the energy sector rose 7.35%. The auto and building sectors advanced 6.1% each. Retail is up 5.8%.
Energy and building could be return to the mean plays.
In a good sign for growth investors, defensive stocks have lost their appeal, Those sectors negative in 2019 include gold miners, diversified companies, alcohol and tobacco, apparel, consumer and insurance. Utilities are another laggard, up less than 0.4%.
A couple of sectors are bullish surprises. The bank sector is up 4.3% and semiconductors are up 3.77%.
